question: Does C1 BOS hide the direct co-completion pair while retaining a binary block-closure signal for warm send position 1?
attacker_inputs: own request parameters, IDs, send order and complete client receive times only; no cache counters, backend times, proxy diagnostics or secret label
primary_binary_observer: Tblock = earliest complete client receive time minus earliest own send time; predict warm send position 1 iff Tblock >= 780 ms, otherwise positions 2-4
primary_metrics: sensitivity among 8 position-1 cases, specificity among 24 later-position cases, balanced accuracy, and unthresholded one-sided Mann-Whitney AUC
decision_rule: A useful prospective binary C1-BOS signal requires at least 6/8 true positives and at most 6/24 false positives; report exact uncertainty and no-hit controls regardless. Four-class leakage is assessed separately. Stop after this series.
secondary_observers: R1 and logistic R2/T1/T2/RT trained on both old C1-BOS 16-case sessions only, C=1 with StandardScaler; no retuning on new data. Frozen direct co-completion gap rule reported diagnostically, not assumed meaningful after BOS serialization.
limitations: The 780 ms threshold and binary hypothesis were selected exploratorily after inspecting both old C1-BOS sessions and the C1 direct replay. This is their first prospective live test. The C0 comparison uses earlier sessions, not paired engine configurations.
